# Memory Leak

Memory leaks are more common than one thinks. Java, despite being a managed
language, it too can suffer from memory leaks, sometime in subtle ways. This
example shows a common pitfall that many Java developers are not aware of.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

- [JDK Mission Control (JMC)](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/javase/products-jmc9-downloads.html)

## JDK Mission Control (JMC)

1. Download the latest version of JMC from
   [here](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/javase/products-jmc9-downloads.html)

2. Specify the version of Java

   When having multiple versions of Java installed, you may need to specify
   which one to be used by JMC. This can be done through the `jmc.ini` file,
   found under the `Eclipse` directory of where JMC is installed.

   Add the `-vm` option followed by the path to the `bin` directory, as shown
   next.

   ```
   ...
   -vm
   /Users/aattard/.sdkman/candidates/java/current/bin
   ...
   ```

   Please note that this file will contain other information, which is excluded
   for brevity.

## Build the application

The following examples require the application to be built.

```shell
./mvnw clean package
```

(*Optional*) Verify that the JAR file was created

```shell
tree --sort=name './target/libs'
```

There should be one JAR file

```
./target/libs
└── memory-leak-1.0.0.jar

1 directory, 1 file
```

Some of the following commands dump JFR files into a `jfr` directory. Make sure
that the `jfr` directory exists.

```shell
rm -rf './jfr'
mkdir -p './jfr'
```

## Create custom configuration

This example will analyse memory leaks. The TLAB (Thread Local Allocation
Buffer) data is not collected by either the *default* nor the *profile*
configurations. This provides insight on how memory is being used by the
application, such as what objects are being created and from where. Create a new
configuration that captures the TLAB’s events.

1. Create the custom configuration

   ```shell
   jfr configure \
     jdk.ObjectAllocationInNewTLAB#enabled=true \
     jdk.ObjectAllocationOutsideTLAB#enabled=true \
     jdk.PromoteObjectInNewPLAB#enabled=true \
     jdk.PromoteObjectOutsidePLAB#enabled=true \
     --output './jfr/custom.jfc'
   ```

   Alternatively, use the interactive option, as shown below, and follow the
   provided instructions.

   ```shell
   jfr configure --interactive --output './jfr/custom.jfc'
   ```

   Select option `4`, to collect the TLAB data, and accept the default for the
   rest.

   ```
   ============== .jfc Configuration Wizard ============
   This wizard will generate a JFR configuration file by
   asking 12 questions. Press ENTER to use the default
   value, or type Q to abort the wizard.

   Garbage Collector: Normal (default)
   1. Off
   2. Normal
   3. Detailed
   4. High, incl. TLABs/PLABs (may cause many events)
   5. All, incl. Heap Statistics (may cause long GCs)
   4
   Using: High, incl. TLABs/PLABs (may cause many events)
   ...
   ```

2. (*Optional*) A `.jfc` file will be created. This file can be saved anywhere
   on the filesystem as long as it is accessible. For this example, the `.jfc`
   is saved under the `jfr` directory.

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './jfr'
   ```

   The custom configuration

   ```
   ./jfr
   └── custom.jfc

   1 directory, 1 file
   ```

   The `.jfr` file is an XML file and can be viewed and edited manually.

## Identify the memory leak

1. Run the application with maximum heap size of 128M (`-Xmx128M`) and using the
   custom JFR configuration (`./jfr/custom.jfc`).

   ```shell
   java \
     -Xms128M \
     -Xmx128M \
     -XX:StartFlightRecording=dumponexit=true,name='Memory-Leak',filename='./jfr/demo-before-fix-128M.jfr',settings='./jfr/custom.jfc' \
     -jar './target/libs/memory-leak-1.0.0.jar'
   ```

   The application will start running until it crashed with an
   `OutOfMemoryError` error, due to its memory leak.

   ```
   [0.231s][info][jfr,startup] Started recording 1. No limit specified, using maxsize=250MB as default.
   [0.231s][info][jfr,startup]
   [0.231s][info][jfr,startup] Use jcmd 123456 JFR.dump name=Memory-Leak to copy recording data to file.
   Number of books in the set 13
   Exception in thread "main" java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
       at demo.Main.main(Main.java:21)
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the JFR file was created.

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './jfr'
   ```

   The recording

   ```
   ./jfr
   ├── custom.jfc
   └── demo-before-fix-128M.jfr

   1 directory, 2 files
   ```

2. Increase the maximum heap size and try again.

   It is not recommended to simply increase the memory of an application without
   first understanding what's happening. We are doing so here, only for
   demonstration purposes. It is highly recommended to first understand why the
   application ran out of memory and only allocate more memory if truly
   necessary.

   ```shell
   java \
     -Xms256M \
     -Xmx256M \
     -XX:StartFlightRecording=dumponexit=true,name='Memory-Leak',filename='./jfr/demo-before-fix-256M.jfr',settings='./jfr/custom.jfc' \
     -jar './target/libs/memory-leak-1.0.0.jar'
   ```

   Unfortunately, this did not resolve the issue. It simply delayed the time
   until the program ran out of memory.

   ```
   [0.226s][info][jfr,startup] Started recording 1. No limit specified, using maxsize=250MB as default.
   [0.226s][info][jfr,startup]
   [0.226s][info][jfr,startup] Use jcmd 123456 JFR.dump name=Memory-Leak to copy recording data to file.
   Number of books in the set 13
   Exception in thread "main" java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
       at java.base/java.util.HashMap.newNode(HashMap.java:1910)
       at java.base/java.util.HashMap.putVal(HashMap.java:638)
       at java.base/java.util.HashMap.putIfAbsent(HashMap.java:1153)
       at demo.Main.main(Main.java:21)
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the JFR file was created.

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './jfr'
   ```

   The recordings

   ```
   ./jfr
   ├── custom.jfc
   ├── demo-before-fix-128M.jfr
   └── demo-before-fix-256M.jfr

   1 directory, 3 files
   ```

3. Open the flight recording in JMC (`./jfr/demo-before-fix-256M.jfr`)

   ```shell
   jmc -open "$(pwd)/jfr/demo-before-fix-256M.jfr"
   ```

   Navigate to the _TLAB Allocations_ and select the _By Class_ tab

   ![TLAB Allocations](./assets/images/JMC%20-%20TLAB%20Allocations%20-%20Before%20Fix.png)

## Address the memory leak

1. Recompile the application

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean compile
   ```

   Look at the compiler warnings!!

   ```
   ...
   [INFO] --- compiler:3.16.0:compile (default-compile) @ memory-leak ---
   [INFO] Recompiling the module because of changed source code.
   [INFO] Compiling 2 source files with javac [debug release 25] to target/classes
   [WARNING] src/main/java/demo/Book.java:[5,14] Class demo.Book overrides equals, but neither it nor any superclass overrides hashCode method
   [INFO] ------------------------------------------------------------------------
   ...
   ```

   As anticipated, the compiler finds a possible issue.

2. Fix the issue pointed out by the compiler.

   ```diff
   @@ -15,4 +15,9 @@ public class Book {
            return object instanceof Book other
                    && Objects.equals(name, other.name);
        }
   +
   +    @Override
   +    public int hashCode() {
   +        return Objects.hashCode(name);
   +    }
    }
   ```

   The [`Book` class](./src/main/java/demo/Book.java) should look like the
   following example.

   ```java
   package demo;

   import java.util.Objects;

   public final class Book {

       private final String name;

       public Book(final String name) {
           this.name = name;
       }

       @Override
       public boolean equals(final Object object) {
           return object instanceof final Book other
                   && Objects.equals(name, other.name);
       }

       @Override
       public int hashCode() {
           return Objects.hashCode(name);
       }
   }
   ```

   Another option is to use records, which also reduce the amount of boilerplate
   code.

3. Rebuild the project

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package
   ```

   This time the compiler will finish without any warnings.

   ```
   ...
   [INFO] --- compiler:3.16.0:compile (default-compile) @ memory-leak ---
   [INFO] Recompiling the module because of changed source code.
   [INFO] Compiling 2 source files with javac [debug release 25] to target/classes
   [INFO]
   [INFO] --- resources:3.4.0:testResources (default-testResources) @ memory-leak ---
   ...
   ```

4. Rerun the application with less memory (`-Xmx64M`)

   ```shell
   java \
     -Xms64M \
     -Xmx64M \
     -XX:StartFlightRecording=dumponexit=true,name='Memory-Leak',filename='./jfr/demo-after-fix-64M.jfr',settings='./jfr/custom.jfc' \
     -jar './target/libs/memory-leak-1.0.0.jar'
   ```

   This time the application completes as expected

   ```
   [0.228s][info][jfr,startup] Started recording 1. No limit specified, using maxsize=250MB as default.
   [0.228s][info][jfr,startup]
   [0.228s][info][jfr,startup] Use jcmd 123456 JFR.dump name=Memory-Leak to copy recording data to file.
   Number of books in the set 13
   Number of books in the map 13
   ```

5. Analyse the flight recording using JMC (`./jfr/demo-after-fix-64M.jfr`)

   ```shell
   jmc -open "$(pwd)/jfr/demo-after-fix-64M.jfr"
   ```

   Navigate to the _TLAB Allocations_ and select the _By Class_ tab

   ![TLAB Allocations](./assets/images/JMC%20-%20TLAB%20Allocations%20-%20After%20Fix.png)

   Please note that we are still creating many unnecessary objects. We can avoid
   that by checking if the book exists in the map and only create it if it does
   not exist.

   ![Garbage Collection](./assets/images/JMC%20-%20Garbage%20Collection%20-%20After%20Fix.png)

   This is a garbage collection problem rather than a memory leave.

   Addressing this can be a bit tricky to solve as we need the `Book` instance
   before we can check whether it exists in the map or not. This problem can be
   addressed by caching the books and only create a new book if an instance does
   not already exist.
